recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5353; future requests for additional identifier-type codes, jurisdiction-specific identifier systems, or further mapping guidance should be handled as separate terminology, registry, or mapping-specification work.
issue_request: FHIR-5353 was a Published FHIR-core/MnM Jan 2015 ballot comment resolved Persuasive with Modification. It requested a clear coded identifier type on Identifier as a 0..1 CodeableConcept with an extensible binding, plus usage notes that the coded type is not a substitute for Identifier.system and should not define codes that are 1..1 with systems.
initial_application: Git history shows the Jira-cited svn r5063 application as commit 0c9b5378687bfa0a80cbf386bbda371a0becc39e, which replaced Identifier.label with Identifier.type as 0..1 CodeableConcept and bound it to IdentifierType. The immediately following build-fix commit f976eec819da795c0bc81e9bef74077506a5a5c2 added the identifier-type value set. Later terminology maintenance moved and refined the value set without removing the requested datatype element or guidance.
additional_context: Identifier is an active datatype in source/fhir.ini and is marked normative. Current source/datatypes/identifier.xml defines Identifier.type as 0..1 CodeableConcept with the IdentifierType binding and guidance that it deals only with general identifier categories and should not correspond 1..1 with Identifier.system. Current source/terminologies/bindings.xml keeps IdentifierType as an extensible binding, source/terminologies/valueset-identifier-type.xml provides the maintained value set, and source/datatypes.html repeats the key narrative guidance. Later FHIR-20466 resolved no-change on the same Identifier.type vs Identifier.system boundary, confirming that Identifier.type is not intended for identifier universality mechanisms or single namespaces; FHIR-20467 is a duplicate of that later issue. Quoted Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current source already preserves the substance of FHIR-5353. The historical request's word "code" is represented in the current specification as Identifier.type, and the current terminology location/value-set representation reflects later maintenance rather than a missing core change.

related_jiras.note: Later MnM no-change decision confirms Identifier.type is for identifier kind/category, not a replacement for Identifier.system or identifier universality mechanisms.
Duplicate of FHIR-20466 on the same Identifier.type/Identifier.system clarification question.
